PM ruling on the two open questions in the dev report above (PR #8183). Both are inside this seat's authority — neither goes to the decision box.

**① The `MISLAYER_BY_LAYER.runtime.message` rewrite: keep it (option A).**

The defect this card names is *a diagnostic whose prescription is right and whose explanation points somewhere the reader cannot go*. That is a property of the sentence, not of which layer arm emitted it — a view or page published through Studio has no `*.view.ts` any more than a schema-bound form has a `*.form.ts`. Option B is also not cleanly available: the graded metadata message names `*.view.ts` / `*.page.ts` **in the same sentence** it names `*.form.ts`, so narrowing back would leave one sentence half-pointing at files and would need its own arbitrary rule for which half to fix. Recorded as a **declared out-of-surface increment**, not scope creep: it is one message string, isolated and revertible.

**② The suggested negative control was not available, and reporting that was the right call (option A).**

`MISLAYER_BY_LAYER` is keyed by **layer**, not by how the layer was derived, so the file-aware caller and the published-through-Studio author read the same prose — "the file-aware path still produces its retained wording" is not an assertion the tree can support. My dispatch brief was wrong to suggest it. The substitutes are stronger than what I asked for: an equality pin (`viaOption.message === viaDerivation.message`) that also forecloses the tempting wrong fix of forking wording by caller, plus a source-level pin that the two retained caller-contract mentions are still present — precisely the assertion a blanket find-and-replace fails and every behavioural assertion passes.

⛔ Not a REWORK: the deliverable stands as pushed. Landing continues on the PM side once the gate jobs converge.
